subject: BYOK proof-of-control & rendezvous plan
messages:
From: BrightWare Security <sec@brightware.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: BYOK onboarding — proof-of-control items + rendezvous

Sergio,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare to onboard BrightWare to a private Redwood deployment (BYOK), our security team needs concrete proof-of-control items and an operational "rendezvous" plan for transferring signed key material. Specifically we need:

- Evidence that customer-supplied keys are held in an HSM-backed KEK and that the operator cannot exfiltrate raw key material.
- A short description of the unseal/transfer ceremony (who signs, what tokens are used, where material is staged).
- Network constraints and the exact port/IP ranges required during the rendezvous window.
- Sample operator availability windows (their ops team is in PST).

Can you provide a filled template and propose two 1-hour windows next week for the handoff? We also need any audit artefacts you can supply (signed public-key fingerprints, attestation statements).

Attached: sample_request_from_customer.txt (stub)

Best,
Chris Patel
Security Lead — BrightWare
chris.patel@brightware.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: BrightWare Security <sec@brightware.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BYOK onboarding — proof-of-control items + rendezvous

Chris — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Soojin (on our private-deploy ops) and Mina (security/compliance) so we can assemble artefacts and schedule the rendezvous.

Short answers up front:
- We will store customer KEKs in an HSM (FIPS 140-2 level 3 equivalent configuration) with split-operator access; raw key material never leaves the HSM.
- The handoff is a staged ceremony: customer generates key locally, exports wrapped key blob (wrapped with HSM public key), uploads to RDC staging bucket, then we perform attestation + import. We will provide signed fingerprints and an attestation statement from the HSM operator.
- Network: rendezvous requires an egress rule for our operator bastion (34.217.45.12; TCP 443) and an inbound ephemeral tunnel for customer-side upload (we provide presigned upload URLs; no open inbound ports to customer infra). Exact CIDR / port list included in the attached checklist.

Attachments I prepared for you (attached here as stubs):
- BYOK-proof-of-control-template.pdf — template we ask customers to complete; includes fields for key origin, wrapping algorithm, and expected lifetime.
- network-rendezvous-checklist.md — operational checklist with IPs, CDN/presigned-url workflow, verification steps.
- operator-availability.csv — rough availability we can offer for the next two weeks.

Action items:
1) Chris — confirm which two windows you prefer from the CSV; we will lock in Soojin's operator and a compliance witness (Mina).
2) Mina — can you draft a short attestation statement (1-2 paragraphs) that we can sign post-import?
3) Ben — please pull any previous signed-fingerprint examples from our artifact store and attach to the final packet.

Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BYOK onboarding — proof-of-control items + rendezvous

Chris / team — thanks, this is actionable. We can support both windows you marked in the CSV: 2026-05-06 14:00-15:00 PST and 2026-05-07 09:00-10:00 PST. I will reserve the operator and a second operator as backup for the first window; Mina will act as compliance witness for both.

Notes / clarifications for the ceremony (short):
- Customer generates RSA-3072 key pair locally and wraps the private key with our HSM public key (RSA-KEM + AES-GCM wrap). We will verify the wrap by checking the provided fingerprint against the one in the attestation statement.
- Transport: customer uploads the wrapped blob to our temporary staging bucket using a presigned PUT URL; the presigned URL expires after 30 minutes. No inbound open ports are required on customer side.
- Operator access: we will use split-signing (2-of-3 threshold) for the import command. Operator work is logged, and we will export a signed audit record (tlog) immediately after import.
- Post-import verification: we will run a test unwrap cycle inside a locked audit session and provide the signed transient-report (PDF) and the operator tlog.

Attached: BYOK-proof-of-control-template.pdf (filled draft), network-rendezvous-checklist.md (finalized), operator-availability.csv (selected slots).

Please confirm the 2026-05-06 slot if that works for your team and we'll send calendar invites + a short runbook.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Ops Engineer — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
